stories.headline: Congress deals twin defeats to Lula: Rejects Supreme Court nominee, overrides sentencing reduction veto
stories.summary: Brazil's Congress dealt President Lula back-to-back defeats within 24 hours this week. The Senate rejected his nomination of Solicitor General Jorge Messias to the Supreme Court—the first rejection of a presidential STF nominee in 132 years—and Congress subsequently overrode his veto of a sentencing reduction bill (PL da Dosimetria) that could reduce ex-president Bolsonaro's 27-year prison sentence. The double loss signals eroded executive power and a strengthened conservative bloc.

The government framed the work schedule reform as a key campaign message ahead of the 2026 election, with union rallies featuring prominent PT figures.

The measure targets household indebtedness as a key government priority heading into elections.

stories.headline: Former president Bolsonaro undergoes shoulder surgery; health recovery progresses
stories.summary: Ex-President Jair Bolsonaro underwent shoulder surgery on May 1st at a Brasília hospital to repair a rotator cuff injury. The procedure lasted approximately 5 hours without complications. Throughout the week, medical bulletins indicated steady recovery with pain management underway and physiotherapy beginning. Bolsonaro remains under house arrest with temporary humanitarian leave, authorized by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes for medical treatment. The surgical recovery allows him to remain active in political advocacy from his condominium.

Sources indicate Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes and Justice André Mendonça coordinated to block Messias's confirmation, citing concerns about the Master bank scandal and judicial power dynamics. The rejection represents a broader institutional crisis, with opposition politicians and analysts warning of STF legitimacy concerns and signaling potential for future judicial reform or impeachment measures against justices. The PT plans legal challenges to both the Messias rejection and the Dosimetria decision.

stories.headline: Petrobras announces record Q1 2026 production; raises prices for gas and jet fuel

The company also announced a new P-79 production platform began operations ahead of schedule on May 1st at the Búzios field in pre-sal Santos Basin. Concurrently, Petrobras increased prices: natural gas by 19.2% and jet fuel (QAV) by 18%, citing international market conditions and contractual formulas tied to Brent crude prices.

stories.headline: Central Bank cuts interest rates by 25 basis points; maintains cautious stance amid global tensions
stories.summary: Brazil's Central Bank (BCB) cut the base interest rate (Selic) by 25 basis points to 14.5% in the May monetary policy meeting, marking the second consecutive cut. The decision was unanimous among the Copom committee. The bank cited external uncertainties, particularly the US-Israel-Iran conflict affecting global markets and oil prices. Finance Minister Haddad and analysts argue the cuts remain insufficient given inflation pressures, while the BCB signals continued caution about future reductions pending new economic data.

stories.headline: Federal government mobilizes disaster response to Pernambuco flooding emergency

President Lula announced federal emergency mobilization, with the Ministry of Integration and Health coordinating disaster response efforts. The government deployed the National Health Force and Civil Defense to affected regions, particularly the Recife metropolitan area and Zona da Mata Norte. Lula personally coordinated with state and local officials to provide immediate aid and establish emergency status declarations.
